content:
Summer AirPods sales are in full swing. Although the next-generation earbuds may be released as soon as within a month, at which point prices could drop further, the AirPods Pro 3 have already fallen to an all-time low, the AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) have also dropped to near their lowest price in six months, and the brand-new AirPods Max 2, originally not expected until 2026, are now discounted by US$120.

Within the next month, Apple is very likely to officially announce its next-generation in-ear personal audio device, but the company had already upgraded its over-ear headphones earlier this year with the launch of the all-new AirPods Max 2, and these new headphones are now selling at an all-time low price.

  • AirPods Pro 3 for US$190 (original price US$249)
  • AirPods Max 2 for US$429 (original price US$549)
  • AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) for US$135 (original price US$179) — the lowest price in six months
  • AirPods 4 for US$99 (original price US$129)

Amazon is currently selling the AirPods Max 2 for US$429 with free shipping, a US$120 discount off the original price of US$549, making it one of the best prices ever since the headphones were launched. Although a brief US$399 deal appeared during Prime Day, stock and colour options were quite limited at the time.

Best Buy is currently selling all five colours at a discount as part of its 60th anniversary promotions that started this morning; Amazon is expected to follow suit shortly.

  • AirPods Max 2 in all colours for US$429 (original price US$549)

Apple finally delivered a true next-generation upgrade to the AirPods Max earlier this year, though when a third generation will arrive remains unknown. The previous model was regarded by many as an AirPods Max 1.5, with main changes being a new look and a USB-C port; but this year's Max 2 brings significant spec upgrades, including high dynamic range amplifiers, and a listening experience powered by the Apple H2 chip — with active noise cancellation performance improved by up to 1.5x, plus brand-new 'digital signal processing algorithms' to enhance Transparency mode performance.

We have covered all the upgrades in detail before; here is a brief overview from Apple:

  • Adaptive Audio: Automatically adjusts the intensity of active noise cancellation and Transparency mode based on the user's surroundings, delivering the best listening experience.
  • Conversation Awareness: Automatically lowers media volume and reduces background noise when the user starts speaking with someone nearby.
  • Live Translation: Powered by Apple Intelligence, this feature helps users communicate face-to-face in different languages.
  • Voice Isolation: Uses advanced computational audio technology driven by the H2 chip to prioritise the user's voice during calls while blocking out ambient noise.
  • Camera Remote: Users can remotely take photos or start and stop video recording via the Camera app on iPhone or iPad, or supported third-party camera apps, by pressing the Digital Crown.
  • Studio-Quality Audio Recording: Allows journalists, podcast hosts, singers, and other creators to record content with higher audio quality and more natural vocal texture.
  • Noise Reduction: Helps users avoid exposure to loud environmental sounds while preserving the tonal characteristics of what they are listening to.
  • Personalised Volume: Automatically fine-tunes the listening experience based on the user's long-term preferences.
  • Siri Interactions: Users can simply nod to say 'yes' or shake their head to say 'no' to easily and privately respond to Siri prompts.
